ModMetaData.name: Props as Style
ModMetaData.author: Nelim
ModMetaData.description:
Turns furniture and props from other mods into alternative appearances for the vanilla things you already build - as ideoligion styles when a whole themed set lines up, as random graphics when one vanilla thing has many variants.
Nothing new to construct, no new architect entry, no new def of any building. A vanilla bed stays a vanilla bed - same stats, same cost, same behaviour - it just looks like something else, and you pick which at build time or at the styling station.
Currently covered, when the source mod is present: - Outer Rim - Furniture and Decor: three categories, corellian, coruscant and tatooine, eight pieces each. Bed, double bed, dining chair, stool, dresser, end table, 2x2 table and autodoor. - Ponpeco Furnitures Kids' Room: two categories, sixteen styles. A full child's bedroom set, bedroll to royal bed. - Rabbie The Moonrabbit race: two categories, twenty styles. Beds, sofas, chairs, stools, dresser, nightstand, shelf, lamps, flower pot, bookcase and door.
- Chinese Traditional Cultural Things Expanded: one category, five styles. Bedside table, dresser, dining chair, 2x2 and 3x3 tables.
And as random graphics, needing Vanilla Expanded Framework: - Alpha Props - Parks and Gardens: fifteen extra looks for the vanilla plant pot, five for the standing lamp. The vanilla texture stays in the draw, always first.
Each source is gated by LoadFolders, so a mod you do not have costs nothing and errors nothing.
Nine vanilla targets are not styleable out of the box - Bed, DoubleBed, Dresser, EndTable, Bedroll, RoyalBed, AnimalBed, Armchair and Door - so the mod adds the component to them, defensively: it creates the comps node only if missing, and adds the component only if not already there.
Needs Ideology for the style system itself. Style Change Anytime is recommended: without it a style category has to be attached to an ideoligion before you can use it.
No save data of its own.
